newsitem.title: UK: UK minister sees no inflation risk from jobs data.
newsitem.headline: UK minister sees no inflation risk from jobs data.

text.p: UK Employment Minister Eric Forth said he did not believe the sharp drop in unemployment seen in November and December posed a risk of a resurgence in inflation.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, he also said that November and December had been unusually good months and he did not expect unemployment to continue falling at the same rapid pace in the coming months.
"There is undoubtedly now a strong and consistent underlying trend of a fall in unemployment, which is very welcome," Forth said.

"It would seem that at the moment...we have created the economic conditions and environment in which we can see a continuing, steady fall in unemployment but also see inflation well under control," he added.
"At the moment I see no reason to believe that there are limits on that."

Forth said he would not claim that either November's "extraordinary fall" or the very good fall seen in December represented the reality of falling unemployment and job creation as there had been special factors involved.
"I think that they are exceptional months, they are exceptional figures and I would not expect to see similar sorts of figures like that or of that magnitude for the months ahead," he added.
But the downward trend in unemployment remained very solid.
Forth said he expected average earnings to hold steady at current levels of around 4.0 percent year-on-year.
"We now have a stable economic environment," he said.
